Cliché

/klee-SHAY/ — rhymes with bouquet · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A cliché is a phrase or idea that has been repeated so often that it now sounds stale and unoriginal.

The coach avoided the usual clichés and gave a speech no one had heard before.

Worked Example

A graduation speech quotes 'This is the beginning of the rest of your life' and 'Follow your dreams no matter what.'

These are clichés—phrases we've heard so many times in graduation speeches that they've lost their impact and originality. Cliché captures both the repetition and the resulting staleness of the language.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

platitude: a flat remark repeated until meaningless

banality: a dull, unoriginal statement or quality

stereotype: a fixed, oversimplified idea about a group

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

originality: freshness that has never been seen before

novelty: something new, unusual, and unexpected

Where it sits · how worn down by overuse it is — original → familiar → trite → cliché

original vs. cliché: Original is the opposite pole from cliché: an original phrase is fresh and unexpected, while a cliché has been worn smooth by endless repetition.

familiar vs. cliché: Familiar is weaker than cliché: a familiar phrase is simply one you recognize, while a cliché is so overused that it has lost its power entirely.

trite vs. cliché: Trite is the closest neighbor to cliché: both describe stale expressions, but trite is the adjective for worn-out wording, while a cliché is the worn-out phrase itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cliché (from clicher)

Root — cliché (from clicher): 'to click' — the sound of a printing plate stamping identical copies (French)

Put it together

Put it together: French clicher imitated the click of a metal printing plate stamping out identical copies, so a cliché was originally the plate itself. Today a cliché is a phrase 'stamped out' so many times that it sounds stale and unoriginal.

Use the root in a new word: click

Use the root in a new word: click: The old printing plate went click each time it stamped another identical copy — that clicking sound, French clicher, is where cliché comes from.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Cliché is a useful word for identifying overused phrases and ideas in writing and speech. Use it when you want to criticize something for being stale and lacking originality. For more neutral language, use 'familiar' or 'conventional' instead.
